figures.caption: 圖：操場上的跳蚤市場
figures.description: 天氣晴朗的週六上午，學校操場上掛著一條寫著「校園跳蚤市場」的布條，布條下面有三個攤位。左邊的攤位擺著一疊舊書，一個男生拿著一本打開的漫畫翻看。中間的攤位擺著幾件摺好的舊衣服，一個女生拿著一件掛著「100元」價格牌的外套，對站在桌子後面的攤主說：「50元可以嗎？」右邊的攤位擺著一顆球和一台玩具車，兩個學生正在以物換物：一個人拿出一隻玩具熊，另一個人拿出一盒拼圖，兩人都沒有拿錢。

questions.stem: 提示：有些學校會在週末舉辦跳蚤市場，讓學生把用不到的舊書、舊衣服和玩具帶到學校販賣，或是和同學交換。請根據下圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段描述圖中跳蚤市場的情景；第二段說明學生為什麼喜歡參加這類活動，以及跳蚤市場可能帶來的影響。

1.explanation_zh: 第一段描述圖中三個攤位的情景；第二段有兩個任務：學生喜歡參加跳蚤市場的原因，以及跳蚤市場可能帶來的影響。原因可以從賣方與買方兩邊寫；影響可以寫對個人、對學校或對環境的影響，好處、壞處都可以，但要具體。
evidence: 第二段說明學生為什麼喜歡參加這類活動
跳蚤市場可能帶來的影響
1.strategy_zh: 圖中三個攤位各有一個重點：翻書帶出「便宜挖寶」，議價帶出「討價還價的樂趣」，以物換物帶出「不用花錢也能讓東西再被使用」，都可以接到第二段的原因與影響。
hints: 第一段：先寫布條與三個攤位，再依左、中、右寫每個攤位的人在做什麼
第二段前半：兩個原因，其中一個配合自己或同學的經驗
第二段後半：至少一項影響，最後提出自己的見解

moves.zh: 描述圖中跳蚤市場的情景

content.focus_zh: 第一段要寫出布條與三個攤位：翻看漫畫的男生、拿著標價 100 元的外套想用 50 元買下的女生、用玩具熊交換拼圖的兩個學生；第二段要有學生喜歡參加的原因（賺零用錢、用低價買到東西、議價或交換的樂趣、交朋友等）與至少一項影響（減少浪費、珍惜物品、增加交流，或品質、衛生等問題），可以用自己的經驗或具體金額支持。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第一段依攤位由左到右描述；第二段先寫原因再寫影響，影響可以先寫好處再補充需要注意的地方，結尾提出自己的見解。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。
重點排列混亂，前後句常接不起來，讀者不容易跟上。
看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 描述圖片用現在進行式與現在完成式（has picked up），寫經驗用過去式；注意 trade A for B、ask if＋子句的間接問句語序，以及 no longer、instead of＋V-ing 的用法。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。
幾乎沒有正確的句子，無法理解。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 跳蚤市場相關用語（flea market、stall、secondhand、bargain、price tag、trade、swap、pocket money）要用得準；「議價」可以用 bargain 或 ask for a lower price，避免整段只用 buy、sell、things 這幾個字。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The picture shows a flea market on a school sports field on a Saturday morning. Under a large sign, students have set up three tables, and each one offers something different. At the first table, a boy is looking through a comic book from a pile of used books. At the second one, a girl is holding a jacket and bargaining with the seller. The price tag says one hundred dollars, but she is asking if she can pay only fifty. Meanwhile, at the toy table, two students are trading a teddy bear for a puzzle without using any money.
Students enjoy flea markets for several reasons. First, they can sell things that they no longer need and earn some pocket money. Second, they can buy useful items at low prices, and bargaining makes shopping feel like a game. For example, at our school flea market last spring, I sold ten old comic books for two hundred dollars and bought a nearly new backpack for only eighty. Flea markets can also have positive effects on a school. To begin with, used things get a second life instead of becoming trash, so less waste is produced. In addition, students from different classes can make new friends while they trade. However, sellers should make sure that their things are clean and safe to use. In conclusion, a flea market is a small event, but it teaches students to value what they have.

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
On a sunny Saturday morning, a school sports field has been turned into a lively marketplace. Beneath a banner announcing the campus flea market, three stalls stand side by side, each offering a different kind of secondhand treasure. At the book stall, a boy has picked up a comic from a stack of used books and is flipping through it, clearly in no hurry to put it down. Next door, a girl holding a jacket marked NT$100 is trying to talk the seller down to half that price. The most interesting deal, however, is happening at the toy stall, where two students are swapping a teddy bear for a jigsaw puzzle without a single coin changing hands. Everyone in the scene seems to be shopping, but not everyone is spending money.
The popularity of such markets is easy to understand. For sellers, a flea market turns clutter into cash; old novels and outgrown clothes that have been gathering dust suddenly become worth something. For buyers, the appeal lies in the hunt, since nobody knows what bargain might be waiting at the next table. Bargaining adds to the fun, too, because it gives shy students a playful reason to start a conversation. Last spring, for example, I sold a stack of comics I had read many times and used the money to buy a nearly new backpack for just NT$80, which I still carry every day. Beyond the benefits for individual students, the event can change a whole school's habits. When students see a sweater or a dictionary find a new owner, they begin to understand that throwing things away is not the only choice. Of course, a flea market is not without problems. Some items may be broken or unclean, and a few sellers may care more about profit than about sharing. Even so, simple rules, such as checking every item before the sale, can easily prevent these problems. In the long run, a few hours of trading may teach students a lesson that no textbook can: the things we own can serve more than one person.

notes.text: the appeal lies in the hunt
without a single coin changing hands

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 描述三個攤位的細節完整，並以「人人在買，卻不是人人在花錢」收束；第二段從賣方與買方分析原因，以 NT$80 買背包的經驗佐證，再由個人延伸到全校的習慣，讓步承認品質與營利問題後提出規則，結尾提出見解（內容 5）；原因、經驗、影響、讓步、結論的順序清楚，轉承多樣（組織 5）；關係副詞 where、without＋受詞＋V-ing、過去完成式皆正確（文法句構 5）；用字生動（clutter、outgrown、bargain），但仍以常用字為主（字彙拼字 4）。總分 19，屬頂標版。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段依左到右寫出布條、翻漫畫的男生、拿 100 元外套議價 50 元的女生與以玩具熊換拼圖的兩人；第二段原因（賣掉不用的東西賺零用錢、低價購物與議價樂趣）與影響（減少浪費、交朋友、清潔安全的提醒）齊全，有具體金額的親身經驗。文法無誤，轉承清楚但偏制式（First、Second、To begin with、In addition），things 稍有重複，屬穩健程度。

top.comment_zh: 描述生動且完整（banner、three stalls、talk the seller down to half that price、swapping … without a single coin changing hands），以 not everyone is spending money 收束第一段；第二段從賣方、買方、議價社交三面說明原因，再寫改變學校習慣的影響並讓步提出品質衛生問題與解方，結尾點題。句型多變、用字精準（clutter into cash、the appeal lies in the hunt），無錯誤。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段依序寫出三個攤位（翻漫畫的男生、100 元外套想付 50 元的女生、以玩具熊換拼圖）；第二段列出原因（零用錢、低價、議價樂趣）與影響（減少浪費、交朋友、衛生提醒），並有賣漫畫買背包的金額舉例。內容完整、無文法錯誤，但影響部分只點到、細節較少，things、buy、sell 重複，轉承語偏制式。

top.comment_zh: 第一段由布條寫到三個攤位並以「不是每個人都在花錢」收尾；第二段賣家、買家、議價、經驗（NT$80 背包）、對學校習慣的影響、可能的問題與解決辦法依序展開，結尾有見解。句型多變，secondhand、bargain、swap、clutter into cash 等用字精準，未見錯誤。
